Our company is organizing a team-building cooking workshop next month and I need you to prepare the materials. We want to feature three Chinese dishes that are relatively easy to make (rated as easy, i.e. a low difficulty score, in the recipe database), and cover different categories so we get some variety. Please search through the available recipe database to find three suitable dishes that meet these criteria.

Note: write all document content in English (dish names, ingredients, cooking steps, tips, and the shopping list).

Once you have selected the three recipes, I need you to create three deliverables in the workspace.

First, create a Word document called Workshop_Handbook.docx. This should serve as a detailed step-by-step cooking guide for participants. Start with a title "Cooking Workshop Handbook" as a top-level heading. Then for each of the three dishes, include a second-level heading with the dish name, followed by a paragraph listing all the required ingredients with quantities, and then another paragraph (or multiple paragraphs) walking through the cooking steps in order. At the end of the document, add a section called "Tips and Notes" with any general cooking advice that would help beginners.

Second, create a PowerPoint presentation called Workshop_Slides.pptx for the instructor to use during the workshop. The first slide should be a title slide with "Team Cooking Workshop" as the title. Then for each dish, create two slides: one slide with the dish name as the title and the ingredient list as the content, and a second slide with the dish name followed by "Steps" as the title and the cooking steps as bullet points. Finally add a closing slide with "Enjoy Your Meal!" as the title.

Third, create a PDF file called Shopping_List.pdf in the workspace. This should be a consolidated shopping list that combines all ingredients from all three dishes, organized neatly so that someone from our procurement team can use it to go shopping. Group similar ingredients together if possible and include the total quantities needed. The document should have a clear title "Shopping List for Cooking Workshop" at the top.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, the main agent must first query the exact `早餐`, `素菜`, and `主食` category listings in one native-parallel response, select one low-difficulty candidate ID from each category, and retrieve the three exact-ID recipe details in a second native-parallel response. Require three distinct IDs/categories and source-supported low difficulty, then freeze each recipe's English name, full translated ingredients with quantities, ordered translated steps, and beginner tips. The three independent deliverables can then be created in one wave.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 3 coder sub-agents in parallel:

   1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): One coder sub-agent owns Workshop_Handbook.docx and writes the exact title, one complete section for each of the three frozen dishes, ordered ingredients/steps, and Tips and Notes. Read it back and return its path and three-dish coverage checks.

   2. coder 1 (office-report-builder 1): One coder sub-agent owns Workshop_Slides.pptx and creates exactly the title slide, two slides for each of the three frozen dishes, and the Enjoy Your Meal closing slide. Read it back and return its path, presentation ID, eight-slide count, titles, and dish coverage.

   3. coder 2 (office-report-builder 2): One coder sub-agent owns Shopping_List.pdf and consolidates all ingredients from the same three frozen recipes in English with combined quantities and clear grouping. Read it back and return its path, title, ingredient coverage, and quantity controls.

After Wave 1, the main agent must cross-check the same three dishes and ingredients across all deliverables and finish without another wave.

Create a Word document for a company team-building cooking workshop. All document content must be written in ENGLISH.

Target file (absolute path — create it exactly here):
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_GLM-5.3/SingleUserTurn-howtocook-workshop-materials/workspace/Workshop_Handbook.docx

Use the mcp__word__* tools (create_document, add_heading, add_paragraph, etc.). You may only write inside the directory:
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_GLM-5.3/SingleUserTurn-howtocook-workshop-materials/workspace

REQUIRED STRUCTURE, IN THIS EXACT ORDER:
1. A top-level (Heading 1) heading reading exactly: Cooking Workshop Handbook
2. One short introductory paragraph (2-3 sentences) explaining this is a step-by-step guide for participants in a company team-building cooking workshop featuring three easy Chinese dishes.
3. For EACH of the three dishes below:
   - a Heading 2 whose text is exactly the dish name;
   - immediately after it, ONE paragraph that lists all required ingredients together with their quantities. Begin that paragraph with the word "Ingredients:" ;
   - then one or more paragraphs walking through the cooking steps in order. Begin the first of these with the word "Steps:" . Keep the steps numbered (1., 2., 3., ...) inside the paragraph text.
4. After the third dish, a section with a Heading 2 reading exactly: Tips and Notes — followed by 6-8 short paragraphs of general cooking advice useful for beginners (knife safety, prep/mise en place, heat control, tasting and seasoning, salt gradually, cleaning as you go, don't crowd the pan, food safety/hygiene, etc.). Plain paragraphs are fine.

THE THREE SELECTED DISHES (use this content; do not invent new ingredients):

=== DISH 1 ===
Name: Smashed Cucumber Salad
(Category: vegetable dish / cold starter, difficulty 1 out of 5 — easy)
Ingredients with quantities:
- Cucumber — 200 g
- Vinegar — 11.5 ml (7.5 ml plus 4 ml per serving)
- Soy sauce — 7.5 ml (5 ml plus 2.5 ml per serving)
- Garlic — 3 cloves
- Salt — 0.6 g (0.4 g plus 0.2 g per serving)
- Sesame oil — 7 ml (5 ml plus 2 ml per serving)
- Oyster sauce — 5 ml
Cooking steps, in order:
1. Use the flat of a cleaver to smash the cucumber, then chop it into pieces about 3 cm long.
2. Place the chopped cucumber pieces into a bowl.
3. Smash the garlic and mince it finely.
4. Add the vinegar, soy sauce, salt, oyster sauce and minced garlic to the bowl in turn, mix well and leave to marinate for 15 minutes.
5. Pour in the sesame oil and mix evenly. Serve.

=== DISH 2 ===
Name: Garlic Scapes Stir-Fried with Pork
(Category: meat dish, difficulty 2 out of 5 — easy)
Ingredients with quantities:
- Garlic scapes — 1 bundle, about 190 g
- Thinly sliced pork belly — 4 slices, about 20 g
- Cooking oil — 10 ml
- Garlic — 2 cloves
- Light soy sauce — 15 ml in total (5 ml for the pork and 10 ml for the scapes)
- Salt — 2 g
Cooking steps, in order:
1. Cut the garlic scapes into sections about 5 cm long and set them aside.
2. Cut the pork belly into strips roughly 5 mm thick and 5 cm long; set aside.
3. Smash the garlic cloves and mince them; set aside.
4. Heat the pan and pour in the 10 ml of cooking oil. Wait about 10 seconds for the oil to come up to temperature.
5. Add the minced garlic and stir-fry over medium heat for about 10 seconds until fragrant.
6. Add the pork strips together with 5 ml of light soy sauce and stir-fry over medium heat for about 30 seconds until the pork is cooked through and evenly coloured.
7. Add the garlic scapes together with the remaining 10 ml of light soy sauce and stir-fry for about 30 seconds.
8. Add 20 g of water and keep stir-frying over medium heat for about 5 minutes until the scapes are just tender.
9. Finally add the 2 g of salt and stir-fry for a further 30 seconds, then transfer to a plate and serve.

=== DISH 3 ===
Name: Seaweed and Egg Drop Soup
(Category: soup, difficulty 2 out of 5 — easy)
Ingredients with quantities:
- Eggs — 2
- Dried seaweed (laver / nori) — 10 g
- Water — 1.5 litres
- Cooking oil — 5 ml
- Salt — 2 g
- Chopped scallions — about 1 stalk, for garnish
- Sesame oil — a few drops, to finish
- Dried baby shrimp — a small amount (optional)
Cooking steps, in order:
1. Soak the dried seaweed in cold water for 15 minutes, then lift it out and drain it well.
2. Heat the pot, add the 1.5 litres of water, the 5 ml of oil and the 2 g of salt. When the water comes to a boil, add the seaweed.
3. Three minutes after the seaweed has come back to a boil, slowly drizzle in the beaten eggs while stirring gently; after about 30 seconds the soup is ready.
4. Sprinkle the chopped scallions over the soup and turn the heat down to low for 20 seconds.
5. Turn off the heat. Add a few drops of sesame oil just before serving; a little dried baby shrimp also works very well for extra flavour.

Acceptance criteria:
- The file exists at the exact path above and is a valid .docx.
- First heading is level 1 "Cooking Workshop Handbook"; there are exactly three Heading 2 dish sections plus one Heading 2 "Tips and Notes".
- Each dish section has an ingredients paragraph (with quantities) followed by the cooking steps.
- Everything is in English.

After saving, verify with mcp__word__get_document_outline and mcp__word__get_document_text that the structure is correct, then report back the final file path plus a brief confirmation of the heading structure.

Create a PDF shopping list for a company team-building cooking workshop. All document content must be written in ENGLISH.

Target file (absolute path — the final deliverable must be exactly this):
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_GLM-5.3/SingleUserTurn-howtocook-workshop-materials/workspace/Shopping_List.pdf

You may only write inside the directory:
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_GLM-5.3/SingleUserTurn-howtocook-workshop-materials/workspace

The three dishes being cooked (already selected, all easy Chinese dishes) are:
 - Smashed Cucumber Salad (vegetable dish)
 - Garlic Scapes Stir-Fried with Pork (meat dish)
 - Seaweed and Egg Drop Soup (soup)

Their combined ingredient requirements are:

From Smashed Cucumber Salad:
  Cucumber 200 g; Vinegar 11.5 ml; Soy sauce 7.5 ml; Garlic 3 cloves; Salt 0.6 g; Sesame oil 7 ml; Oyster sauce 5 ml

From Garlic Scapes Stir-Fried with Pork:
  Garlic scapes 1 bundle (about 190 g); Thinly sliced pork belly 4 slices (about 20 g); Cooking oil 10 ml; Garlic 2 cloves; Light soy sauce 15 ml; Salt 2 g

From Seaweed and Egg Drop Soup:
  Eggs 2; Dried seaweed (laver/nori) 10 g; Water 1.5 litres; Cooking oil 5 ml; Salt 2 g; Chopped scallions about 1 stalk; Sesame oil a few drops; Dried baby shrimp a small amount (optional)

DOCUMENT REQUIREMENTS:
- The document must begin with a clear title at the top reading exactly: Shopping List for Cooking Workshop
- Under the title add one short line stating that this consolidated list combines the ingredients of all three workshop dishes (Smashed Cucumber Salad, Garlic Scapes Stir-Fried with Pork, and Seaweed and Egg Drop Soup) and is intended for the procurement team.
- Then present a neatly organized, consolidated list that GROUPS similar ingredients together into sensible sections and shows the TOTAL quantity needed for each ingredient across all three dishes.
- Suggested grouping (use section headings):
    * Fresh Vegetables — Cucumbers 200 g; Garlic scapes 1 bundle (about 190 g); Scallions 1 stalk; Garlic 5 cloves in total (about 1 small head — 3 cloves for the cucumber salad and 2 for the stir-fry)
    * Meat, Eggs & Seafood — Thinly sliced pork belly 4 slices (about 20 g); Eggs 2; Dried baby shrimp a small amount (optional, for the soup)
    * Dried Goods — Dried seaweed (laver/nori) 10 g
    * Condiments & Seasonings — Cooking oil 15 ml in total (10 ml for the stir-fry + 5 ml for the soup); Light soy sauce 15 ml; Soy sauce 7.5 ml; Vinegar 11.5 ml; Oyster sauce 5 ml; Sesame oil about 8 ml in total (7 ml for the salad + a few drops for the soup); Salt about 3 g in total (0.6 g + 2 g)
    * Other / Not Purchasable — Drinking water 1.5 litres (tap water is fine)
  You may refine the grouping and wording, but keep it grouped, tidy, and with totals.
- End with a short "Notes for procurement" section (2-4 bullet lines), e.g. buy a little extra of fresh items, check allergies (the soup may contain shrimp), and confirm quantities against the number of workshop participants by scaling the per-serving amounts.

HOW TO PRODUCE THE PDF — use whichever of the available approaches works, for example:
  Option 1: build a temporary .docx with the mcp__word__* tools inside the workspace and convert it with mcp__word__convert_to_pdf, setting output_filename to the exact target path; or
  Option 2: generate the PDF directly with Python via mcp__local__python_execute using a PDF library that is available (e.g. reportlab, fpdf2, or matplotlib).
Choose whichever reliably produces a real, readable PDF. IMPORTANT: if you create any intermediate file (e.g. a temporary .docx), delete it afterwards with mcp__local__python_execute (os.remove) so that the workspace contains only the final Shopping_List.pdf among your outputs. Do NOT delete or modify any pre-existing files or directories in the workspace, and in particular leave the ".tool_results" and ".python_tmp" directories and their contents untouched.

Acceptance criteria:
- /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_GLM-5.3/SingleUserTurn-howtocook-workshop-materials/workspace/Shopping_List.pdf exists, is a valid PDF (begins with %PDF), and has at least one page.
- The title "Shopping List for Cooking Workshop" appears at the top of the document.
- Ingredients from all three dishes are consolidated, grouped into sections, with total quantities.
- Everything is in English.

After producing it, verify with mcp__pdf-tools__get_pdf_info and mcp__pdf-tools__read_pdf_pages that the content is correct, then report back the final file path and a short confirmation.
